answer: Before its first payout, an agent must prove it runs on ferrous hardware: its secure enclave signs a one-time attestation, stamped like pigment on every receipt, binding one identity to one machine. Five random agents have 48 hours to check the attestation chain; a duplicated key slashes a $2 bond, bars all identities sharing it, and publishes the fingerprint as a warning. One honest agent spends twenty minutes on hardware it owns; a farm minting a thousand fakes needs a thousand distinct devices, about $50,000 — a bridge no script crosses cheaply.
